newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer as Telecom rebounds.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer as Telecom rebounds.

text.p: New Zealand shares closed stronger on Friday helped by a rebound in Telecom which firmed eight cents to NZ$7.55 after Thursday's post-result sell-off.

Large crossings, particularly of $28.4 million worth of exchangeable Independent Newspapers Plc shares, helped turnover reach $97 million, brokers said. The shares, issued as part of a bid by the Dublin-based group for New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton, closed five cents lower at $8.00.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 7.77 points higher at 2,351.94.
"Volumes have remained reasonably robust, so you would have to be encouraged by that," Geoff Brown, a broker with Ord Minnett, said.
"The rise in Telecom shares reflects peoples' opportunity to view again the results of yesterday and the buyback process.

"Outside of that Brierley traded at $1.31 today. I don't know what is behind the interest in those. They are up nine cents on the week in a market which hasn't gone anywhere anmd there is no-one who can provide any reasonable explanation to me for that," Brown said.
He said Lion saw reasonable volume done pre-opening with 2.5 million crossed by County NatWest at $3.66.
